title: Milton council to draw up resolution on Route 5 speed change | Cape Gazette
text:
Milton Town Council is working up a resolution to be sent to the Delaware Department of Transportation requesting that a section of Harbeson Road between the entrances to Heritage Creek be changed from a 50 mph speed limit to 35 mph. Council will debate the resolution at its Monday, Oct. 5 meeting. NICK ROTH PHOTO

Milton Town Council has agreed to move forward with drawing up a resolution requesting the Delaware Department of Transportation to lower the speed limit on Harbeson Road from 50 mph to 35 mph between the two entrances to Heritage Creek.
Because the road is owned by the state, any changes to the speed limit need to go through DelDOT, but a resolution from council would at least put the request on the table.
In a letter to council, Jeffrey Fernbach, president of Fernmoor Homes, which owns Heritage Creek, said while excessive speeding is not a pervasive issue in the area, vehicles do occasionally travel at speeds that create safety concerns for residents. The request is to lower the speed limit on Harbeson Road between the entrances at Heritage Boulevard and Woodland Avenue.
At council’s Sept. 14 meeting, Nathan Walter, representing Fernmoor, said the area near Heritage Creek has a 35 mph speed limit, so this would be an extension farther south. He said the change would help encourage walking and biking by residents around the entrances.
Mayor John Collier said a resolution would be available by council’s next meeting, scheduled for Monday, Oct. 5. Collier advised the Fernmoor representatives that even if the matter passes council, it will take some time for DelDOT to actually make the change.
